key_insight: The paper introduces automated running error analysis inside finite element kernels so rounding error is estimated alongside the computed value, helping catch instability before it corrupts results.
engineering_relevance: This gives FEM developers a practical debugging and robustness tool for mixed-precision, embedded, and automatically generated PDE kernels where floating-point error can silently dominate.
method: Wrap kernel arithmetic in a custom type that propagates both value and forward error estimate.
Integrate the approach into the FEniCS Form Compiler (FFCx) via a C++ backend and templated type-generic kernels.
Use the error estimates to diagnose cancellation and near-degenerate-mesh sensitivity during assembly.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports two demonstrations—catastrophic cancellation in Neo-Hooke assembly and a near-degenerate Laplace mesh test—and says the implementation typically adds only 2–4x runtime overhead.
watch_item: The approach adds nontrivial performance overhead and depends on a compiler/backend integration path, so deployment complexity and kernel-specific tuning may matter.
paper_title: Running error bounds in finite element kernels
